correctness.rationale: All automorphisms are parameterized bijectively by a nonzero linear coefficient and three arbitrary coefficients, giving \((q-1)q^3\) elements. The induced radical matrix has entries determined by expanding powers through degree four. Full fixed dimension equals five minus \(\operatorname{rank}(M-I)\). Diagonal root strata exhaust a not equal to one, with quadratic resonance \(c=-b^2\) at \(a=-1\); the complete \(a=1\) rank block R has characteristic-dependent ranks (3,2,1,0), (2,2,1,0), (2,1,1,0) for \(p\ge5\), \(p=3\), \(p=2\). Counting all parameter strata gives the precise \(N_1,\ldots,N_5\) formulas, which sum to the group order and whose Burnside sums yield the three orbit formulas. Gaussian-elimination enumeration exhausts each substitution for \(q\in\{2,3,4,5,7,8,9,11,13,16\}\) and direct element-orbit counts verify 14,27,52 at \(q=2,3,4\). Small-field checks corroborate but cannot prove the general case; the symbolic exhaustive rank trichotomy handles all prime powers and boundary roots.

value.rationale: The invariant is a natural complete fixed-space spectrum of the full automorphism group of the first one-variable length-five jet exhibiting the nontrivial \(a=-1\) quadratic resonance. It determines the Burnside element-orbit census, including sharp characteristic-dependent transition from linear to quadratic growth and explicit dependence on cube/fourth roots in the base field. This is an interpretable structural boundary for a canonical finite quotient of formal substitution groups, not an arbitrary single coefficient assignment or a mere re-evaluation of the known automorphism order. Its exact rank-fiber table gives a reusable finite representation invariant and natural base case for higher-order jet orbit problems, without asserting any unproved downstream theorem.
